question: Should experimental Claws be permitted to register manifest-provided MCP servers in globally shared host configuration, and if so what broker, environment, namespace, and explicit-sharing policy is required?
rationale: The code can be mechanically adjusted only after maintainers choose whether this feature owns a privileged host-level capability or must route through a different owner boundary.

options.title: Require host-controlled MCP brokering
options.body: Keep the capability only with an allowlisted or brokered command path, explicit child-environment policy, per-Claw scoping, and host-authorized sharing.

options.title: Narrow to non-executable ownership
options.body: Allow only a constrained declaration class that does not create a new arbitrary local-process execution path.

options.title: Pause this lifecycle slice
options.body: Defer the PR until the Claws RFC and the canonical MCP ownership boundary are accepted.

recommendation.title: Require host-controlled MCP brokering
recommendation.body: Keep the capability only with an allowlisted or brokered command path, explicit child-environment policy, per-Claw scoping, and host-authorized sharing.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and have already reviewed the precise source-config and lifecycle safety boundary.
